# Support

DataQ is free, open-source software (MIT) that you run yourself. Support is given by the
community and the maintainer on a best-effort basis. There is no service-level agreement and
no paid support tier.

## Where to go

| You have | Go to |
|---|---|
| A question about installing, configuring or using DataQ | The [documentation](https://theurgicduke771.github.io/DataQ/docs/latest/), then [Troubleshooting](https://theurgicduke771.github.io/DataQ/docs/latest/operate/troubleshooting/) and the [Runbook & FAQ](https://theurgicduke771.github.io/DataQ/docs/latest/operate/runbook-faq/) |
| A bug, or a question the documentation does not answer | [Open an issue](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/new/choose) |
| A feature request | [Open an issue](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/new/choose) describing the problem you want solved |
| A security vulnerability | **Not** a public issue. Follow the [security policy](SECURITY.md) |

## What helps us help you

- The DataQ version (the image tag or commit you run) and how it is deployed (the
  prebuilt-image stack, Azure, AWS, or from source).
- What you did, what you expected and what happened instead.
- The `request_id` shown on an error page or returned in an API error. It finds the matching
  log lines.
- Logs with secrets removed. DataQ redacts credentials and sample values in its own logs, but
  check anything you paste.

## Which versions get fixes

The latest tagged release and `main`. See the
[supported versions](SECURITY.md#supported-versions) table.
